thesis: Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO) designs and supplies semiconductor devices and infrastructure software for enterprises, cloud operators, and equipment makers. **[Fact]** The company reports two segments: semiconductor solutions (networking, broadband, storage, custom AI accelerators, and wireless) and infrastructure software (VMware private cloud, mainframe, cybersecurity, and fibre-channel storage networking). **[Fact]** Fiscal year 2025 revenue was **$63.9 billion**, up **24%** from **$51.6 billion** in fiscal 2024, with semiconductor solutions at **$36.9 billion** and infrastructure software at **$27.0 billion**. **[Fact]** The VMware acquisition closed **November 22, 2023** for roughly **$30.8 billion** in cash plus **544 million** Broadcom shares. **[Inference]** Broadcom is a serial acquirer turned dual-engine compounder: high-margin silicon tied to data-center and AI build-outs, plus recurring subscription software, funded in part by **~$62 billion** of long-term debt.
why_market_wrong: The market may be capitalizing AI custom-silicon backlog and VMware subscription momentum at a price that already embeds years of owner-cash growth. **[Fact]** Remaining performance obligations were **~$164.6 billion** as of **May 3, 2026**, including a long-term custom AI accelerator contract signed in Q2 fiscal 2026. **[Inference]** If incremental returns on reinvestment fall short of what the stock price implies, or if debt amortization and stock-based compensation absorb more cash than the headline operating cash flow suggests, the equity could remain rich despite strong reported growth. **[Inference]** Conversely, the market could be underweighting how much of fiscal 2025 software revenue came from upfront license recognition (**$7.8 billion** in products revenue) rather than recurring subscription cash.
